## Overview Roll back a newly registered NIXL agent when descriptor preparation fails in the P2P KV-offload transport. Related to #63602, gap 4 only. AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for investigation, implementation, tests, and this description. The human submitter confirmed completion of manual review and authorized submission. The reviewed contribution carries their DCO sign-off. Original-submission results below are the recorded server runs; review follow-up results are the recorded local runs. No additional human test execution is asserted. ## Claims - A failure in `get_xfer_descs` or `prep_xfer_dlist` rolls back the unpublished remote registration. - A failed repeat using already-published native metadata leaves that registration owned by its existing peer. - Cleanup failure is logged without replacing the original registration exception. Native cleanup success cannot be guaranteed when NIXL itself rejects removal. ## Validation The table and native validation below describe the original submission, `18349008c`; follow-up results are recorded separately below. Base: `a7407ab44557802ca32a0ba2c2707362d7d21563`. | Check | Base | Changed | | --- | --- | --- | | Eight new constructor-based cases | 6 failed, 2 passed | 8 passed | | Complete data-transport file | Not measured | 64 passed | | Data transport, sessions, ZMQ transport | Not measured | 223 passed | | Full P2P suite, including manager | Not measured | 319 passed | | Native NIXL 1.5.0 DRAM/UCX reproducer | Metadata survives descriptor failure | Rollback succeeds; 6 real WRITE byte comparisons pass | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | Not measured | Passed, including pinned Ruff, mypy, and test tethering | ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_zmq_transport.py -q .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py ``` Tests construct the real `NixlTransport`; only the external NIXL boundary is mocked. Native validation uses the production transport with two real NIXL agents, host buffers, UCX TCP/shared memory/CUDA-copy, injected descriptor failures, native metadata queries, retries, and exact byte comparisons. Both descriptor stages and an idempotent repeat are checked. This source-level Python validation used Python 3.12.3 and the server's existing torch 2.12.1+cu130. It did not build main's torch 2.14 native extensions. The command excludes the heavyweight root `tests/conftest.py`, and uses the P2P suite's real conftest. No LLM/OpenAI serving run, output-quality evaluation, or RDMA/multi-node fault injection was performed; those are not implied by the transport results. ## Review follow-up — sync registration Commit `6ed41ccf1b` routes `add_remote_peer()` through `add_remote_peer_async(...).result()`, so synchronous and asynchronous builds share the single registration worker. Superseded synchronous registrations now raise, and the rollback check documents its serialization requirement. Validation of this follow-up used macOS/Python 3.12 with the real `NixlTransport` constructor and a mocked external NIXL boundary: | Check | Original PR `18349008c` | With follow-up | | --- | --- | --- | | Race regression plus sync/async superseded-registration cases | 2 failed, 1 passed | 3 passed within the full suite | | Complete data-transport file | 64 passed before adding the regressions | 66 passed | | Full P2P suite | Previously recorded server result: 319 passed | 321 passed | | Applicable pre-commit hooks | Previously passed | Passed, including pinned Ruff, mypy, and test tethering | The before-fix failures were `assert set() == {'peer'}` (the newer registration's agent was removed) and `Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError` (superseded sync registration returned silently). ```bash # With the final tests and original nixl.py from 18349008c: .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py \ -k 'failed_registration_keeps_newer_sync_agent or registration_landing_after_remove_is_discarded' -q # 2 failed, 1 passed, 63 deselected # With the follow-up: .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p -q # 321 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/data/nixl.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_data_transport.py # All applicable hooks passed ``` Both baseline and changed runs emit the same missing generated `vllm._version` warning. No new native-NIXL/RDMA or serving validation is claimed for this follow-up. The already-existing dlist replacement leak remains outside this PR. ## Details The registration worker can register native metadata and then fail before `_publish_peer` records cleanup ownership. `_build_peer_handles` now uses the existing independent teardown helper on that exception path, while preserving the exception and avoiding removal of an already-published native name. All registration builds now use the existing single-worker executor, including the synchronous entry point; the generation/publish flow is unchanged. No steady-state inference work, synchronization, public option, or model arithmetic is added. Duplicate checks covered the issue discussion, open PRs referencing #63602, and P2P/NIXL rollback keywords. #59524 fixes incomplete registration in the separate KV connector `nixl/base_worker.py`; this change fixes the P2P secondary-tier transport. #61667 covers consumer-slot quarantine for unconfirmed writes. Contributor `tejachavali` expressed interest in the broader issue; this PR does not claim assignment or close the full issue. The existing Buildkite `v1-kv-offload` step selects the data-transport tests via `pytest -v -s v1/kv_offload`, and its source dependencies include `vllm/v1/` and `tests/v1/kv_offload`. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Reuses existing cleanup and limits changes to the P2P registration failure path. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Regression and native transport evidence, reproduction commands, and untested configurations are recorded; the submitter confirmed completion of manual review. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Applicable pre-commit hooks pass; no new user configuration or model behavior is introduced. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Scope, duplication checks, evidence, and limitations are explicit.

The published-name check leaves a window when the synchronous `add_remote_peer` runs alongside an async registration for the same peer. If the older registration fails after the newer one has called `add_remote_agent()` but before its `_publish_peer`, the name is not published yet, so the rollback removes the agent the newer registration then publishes. The transport ends up with a published dlist for an agent that no longer exists. Reproduced at `18349008c` with the real `NixlTransport` constructor and a fake external agent: ``` B entered prep while A was blocked: True published={'peer:1': 'nixl-peer-name'} registered=set() AssertionError: published agent was removed ``` The P2P session only calls `add_remote_peer_async`, so this is an API-level race, not a path production hits today. Wonder if we could also route the synchronous `add_remote_peer` through `_reg_executor`: async registrations are already serialized there, so the published-name check and the rollback would both finish before the next build starts. The synchronous call would then raise when superseded, as the async one does. Probe below in case it is useful as a regression test.
test_probe_window.py ```python """Older failed registration A rolls back while newer sync registration B has added the agent but not yet published it.""" import threading from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch import numpy as np from vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.data.nixl import NixlTransport def test_rollback_while_newer_registration_is_building(): agent = MagicMock() with ( patch("vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.data.nixl._NixlAgent", return_value=agent), patch("vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.p2p.data.nixl._NixlAgentConfig"), ): transport = NixlTransport("test:1", memoryview(np.zeros((8, 1024), dtype=np.uint8))) registered: set[str] = set() def add_remote_agent(metadata): registered.add("nixl-peer-name") return "nixl-peer-name" a_in_prep, release_a = threading.Event(), threading.Event() b_in_prep, release_b = threading.Event(), threading.Event() calls = 0 def prep_xfer_dlist(*args, **kwargs): nonlocal calls calls += 1 if calls == 1: a_in_prep.set() assert release_a.wait(10) raise RuntimeError("A failed") b_in_prep.set() assert release_b.wait(10) return MagicMock(name="remote_dlist") agent.add_remote_agent.side_effect = add_remote_agent agent.remove_remote_agent.side_effect = registered.discard agent.prep_xfer_dlist.side_effect = prep_xfer_dlist errors = [] def register_b(): try: transport.add_remote_peer("peer:1", b"meta", 0x1000, 8, 1024) except BaseException as exc: errors.append(exc) try: old = transport.add_remote_peer_async("peer:1", b"meta", 0x1000, 8, 1024) assert a_in_prep.wait(5) transport.remove_remote_peer("peer:1") b = threading.Thread(target=register_b) b.start() concurrent = b_in_prep.wait(1.0) print(f"B entered prep while A was blocked: {concurrent}") release_a.set() try: old.result(timeout=5) except RuntimeError as exc: print(f"A: {exc}") assert b_in_prep.wait(5) release_b.set() b.join(timeout=5) published = dict(transport._peer_nixl_names) print(f"published={published} registered={registered} b_errors={errors}") assert errors == [] assert registered == {"nixl-peer-name"}, "published agent was removed" assert transport.write_blocks("peer:1", [0], [1]) is not None finally: release_a.set() release_b.set() transport.close() ``` Drop it into `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/` and run `pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_probe_window.py -s`.

Thanks, this closes gap 4 cleanly. I checked the rollback against the registration flow on main and ran `test_data_transport.py` locally (64 passed).

The production path looks correct. The session only registers through `add_remote_peer_async`, so every build runs on the single `_reg_executor` worker. Between the `published` check and the release, no other build can publish the same NIXL name. A concurrent `remove_remote_peer` can at worst cause a second `remove_remote_agent`, which `_release_remote_handles` already logs and survives. Re-raising the original exception while `_release_remote_handles` logs cleanup failures is the right split.

Two inline comments: the sync-path race nilig raised, and a small nit.

Not for this PR, just noting it: re-registering a peer that's already published, without removing it first, overwrites `_remote_dlists[peer_id]` in `_publish_peer` and never releases the old dlist handle. That's on main already, so it would be a separate fix.

Agree with nilig's race. I think it's worth fixing here. The rollback's ownership check is only sound because builds run one at a time on `_reg_executor`. This sync path builds on the caller's thread, so it can overlap an async build. An older failed registration can then remove an agent that this call is about to publish. Routing it through the executor removes the gap:

```python
self.add_remote_peer_async(
    peer_id, agent_metadata, base_addr, num_blocks, block_len
).result()
```

Nothing calls this from the registration worker, so it can't deadlock. One behaviour change: a superseded sync registration now raises instead of returning silently. Today it ignores `_publish_peer`'s `False`, which already looks like a bug to me.

Could you add a regression test as well? An older registration fails while a newer one for the same peer has added the agent but not yet published it, and the newer one should stay registered and usable for `write_blocks`.

files.patch:
@@ -6,6 +6,7 @@
 
 import ctypes
 import threading
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
 from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
 
 import numpy as np
@@ -24,6 +25,147 @@ def _remote_disconnect() -> Exception:
     return nixlRemoteDisconnectError("NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT")
 
 
+@pytest.fixture
+def registration_transport():
+    """Track native registrations while constructing the real transport."""
+    agent = MagicMock()
+    registered = set()
+
+    def add_remote_agent(metadata):
+        name = metadata.decode()
+        registered.add(name)
+        return name
+
+    agent.add_remote_agent.side_effect = add_remote_agent
+    agent.remove_remote_agent.side_effect = registered.remove
+    agent.check_xfer_state.return_value = "DONE"
+    with (
+        patch.object(nixl_module, "_NixlAgent", return_value=agent),
+        patch.object(nixl_module, "_NixlAgentConfig"),
+    ):
+        transport = NixlTransport(
+            "test:1", memoryview(np.zeros((8, 1024), dtype=np.uint8))
+        )
+    try:
+        yield transport, agent, registered
+    finally:
+        transport.close()
+
+
+class TestNixlRegistrationRollback:
+    def test_failed_registration_keeps_newer_sync_agent(self, registration_transport):
+        """An older rollback must not remove a newer sync registration's agent."""
+        transport, agent, registered = registration_transport
+        old_preparing, release_old = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
+        new_preparing, release_new = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
+
+        def prep_xfer_dlist(*args, **kwargs):
+            if not old_preparing.is_set():
+                old_preparing.set()
+                assert release_old.wait(timeout=5)
+                raise RuntimeError("old registration failed")
+            new_preparing.set()
+            assert release_new.wait(timeout=5)
+            return MagicMock(name="remote_dlist")
+
+        agent.prep_xfer_dlist.side_effect = prep_xfer_dlist
+        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as caller:
+            try:
+                old = transport.add_remote_peer_async(
+                    "peer:1", b"peer", 0x1000, 8, 1024
+                )
+                assert old_preparing.wait(timeout=5)
+                transport.remove_remote_peer("peer:1")
+                new = caller.submit(
+                    transport.add_remote_peer, "peer:1", b"peer", 0x1000, 8, 1024
+                )
+                # Let an un-serialized sync build reach prep before rollback.
+                # A serialized build waits until the old registration finishes.
+                new_preparing.wait(timeout=1)
+                release_old.set()
+                with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="old registration failed"):
+                    old.result(timeout=5)
+                assert new_preparing.wait(timeout=5)
+                release_new.set()
+                new.result(timeout=5)
+
+                assert registered == {"peer"}
+                transfer = transport.write_blocks("peer:1", [0], [1])
+                assert transfer is not None
+                assert transfer in transport.poll().done
+            finally:
+                release_old.set()
+                release_new.set()
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("asynchronous", [False, True])
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("stage", ["get_xfer_descs", "prep_xfer_dlist"])
+    def test_failed_registration_rolls_back_and_can_retry(
+        self, registration_transport, asynchronous, stage
+    ):
+        """Failed descriptor setup must not leak an agent or damage healthy peers."""
+        transport, agent, registered = registration_transport
+        transport.add_remote_peer("healthy:1", b"healthy", 0x2000, 8, 1024)
+        error = RuntimeError("descriptor setup failed")
+        getattr(agent, stage).side_effect = error
+        register = (
+            transport.add_remote_peer_async
+            if asynchronous
+            else transport.add_remote_peer
+        )
+        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError) as exc_info:
+            result = register("peer:1", b"peer", 0x1000, 8, 1024)
+            if asynchronous:
+                result.result(timeout=5)
+        assert exc_info.value is error
+        assert registered == {"healthy"}
+        assert transport.write_blocks("peer:1", [0], [1]) is None

Agree with nilig's race. I think it's worth fixing here. The rollback's ownership check is only sound because builds run one at a time on `_reg_executor`. This sync path builds on the caller's thread, so it can overlap an async build. An older failed registration can then remove an agent that this call is about to publish. Routing it through the executor removes the gap:

```python
self.add_remote_peer_async(
    peer_id, agent_metadata, base_addr, num_blocks, block_len
).result()
```

Nothing calls this from the registration worker, so it can't deadlock. One behaviour change: a superseded sync registration now raises instead of returning silently. Today it ignores `_publish_peer`'s `False`, which already looks like a bug to me.

Could you add a regression test as well? An older registration fails while a newer one for the same peer has added the agent but not yet published it, and the newer one should stay registered and usable for `write_blocks`.

The published-name check leaves a window when the synchronous `add_remote_peer` runs alongside an async registration for the same peer. If the older registration fails after the newer one has called `add_remote_agent()` but before its `_publish_peer`, the name is not published yet, so the rollback removes the agent the newer registration then publishes. The transport ends up with a published dlist for an agent that no longer exists. Reproduced at `18349008c` with the real `NixlTransport` constructor and a fake external agent: ``` B entered prep while A was blocked: True published={'peer:1': 'nixl-peer-name'} registered=set() AssertionError: published agent was removed ``` The P2P session only calls `add_remote_peer_async`, so this is an API-level race, not a path production hits today. Wonder if we could also route the synchronous `add_remote_peer` through `_reg_executor`: async registrations are already serialized there, so the published-name check and the rollback would both finish before the next build starts. The synchronous call would then raise when superseded, as the async one does. Probe below in case it is useful as a regression test.

Thanks, this closes gap 4 cleanly. I checked the rollback against the registration flow on main and ran `test_data_transport.py` locally (64 passed).

The production path looks correct. The session only registers through `add_remote_peer_async`, so every build runs on the single `_reg_executor` worker. Between the `published` check and the release, no other build can publish the same NIXL name. A concurrent `remove_remote_peer` can at worst cause a second `remove_remote_agent`, which `_release_remote_handles` already logs and survives. Re-raising the original exception while `_release_remote_handles` logs cleanup failures is the right split.

Two inline comments: the sync-path race nilig raised, and a small nit.

Not for this PR, just noting it: re-registering a peer that's already published, without removing it first, overwrites `_remote_dlists[peer_id]` in `_publish_peer` and never releases the old dlist handle. That's on main already, so it would be a separate fix.
Thanks, verified on 6ed41ccf1b: full P2P suite passes (321), and both new tests fail when I revert `nixl.py` to 18349008c9, so they catch the race and the silent superseded sync path. LGTM.
